reason: Start with the after-meal condition to see how pancreatic cells respond to increased blood glucose.
expectation: I expect the pancreatic beta cells to release insulin, though the result may first show a sensing step.

alternatives.reason: The between-meals response is also relevant, but I prefer to follow the meal first.

effect: The result confirms that beta cells release insulin into blood, which carries it to muscle and liver.
reaction: The separate branches make the hormone’s targets clear.
reason: Follow insulin to skeletal muscle to see its role after a meal.
expectation: I expect muscle cells to take up more glucose and possibly store some as glycogen.

alternatives.reason: The liver is another insulin target, but I want to follow the muscle branch first.

effect: Insulin increases muscle glucose entry by increasing membrane transport proteins, and its release signal weakens as blood glucose falls.
reaction: The feedback connection makes the response clearer.
reason: Follow the other insulin branch to see how the liver handles glucose after a meal.
expectation: I expect insulin to promote glucose storage as glycogen in the liver.

alternatives.reason: The between-meals response is relevant, but I want to finish the after-meal branch first.

effect: Insulin favours liver glycogen storage and reduces glucose output, without the muscle-style transporter insertion shown earlier.
reaction: The distinction between liver and muscle responses is useful.
reason: Follow the only available combination to explore the between-meals response.
expectation: I expect lower blood glucose to prompt pancreatic alpha cells to release glucagon.

effect: The between-meals panel confirms increased glucagon release from alpha cells and reduced insulin release, with glucagon reaching the liver.
reaction: The contrast with the after-meal response is clear.
reason: Follow the only available combination to see how the liver maintains blood glucose between meals.
expectation: I expect glucagon to promote glycogen breakdown and glucose release from the liver into blood.

effect: Glucagon promotes liver glycogen breakdown and glucose release; its stimulation diminishes as blood glucose rises. Both goals are complete.
reaction: The feedback closes the between-meals comparison clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following insulin to both muscle and liver was most worthwhile: the picture descriptions distinguish increased muscle transporters from liver glycogen storage rather than presenting identical responses.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate sensing steps were predictable, and after the insulin branches there was only one gameplay combination at each decision.

surprise.text: The explicit contrast between muscle transporter insertion and liver glucose entry sharpened my understanding of the different insulin responses.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the compatible-option menu guided the sequence rather than requiring me to discover the connections.

continue.text: I would continue: comparing opposing hormone responses and their feedback was concise and informative, though the mostly prescribed sequence offered limited decision-making.
